description:
Same class as check-scope-reports-ok-when-no-scope-rules-exist (done), which added --strict for 'the item has no scope rules'. That guard does not cover the other way check-scope can pass without checking anything: an empty or wrong diff.

Both hit for real while landing PRs #1633 and #1635:

(1) Wrong tree. _project/scripts/todo deliberately resolves the tree that owns the shim, not cwd's git toplevel. Running the main clone's shim while the branch lives in a worktree diffs main's HEAD (develop) instead, so it reported 'scope OK (1 changed file(s))' -- one unrelated stray file -- for a 4-file change that actually contained a violation. Re-run from the branch's own worktree it correctly reported the file as outside the only_modify allowlist.

(2) No commits yet. check-scope diffs commits, not the index or working tree. On a fresh branch with staged-but-uncommitted work it reported 'scope OK (0 changed file(s))'.

In both cases the operator sees the word OK and a plausible exit 0. The file count is the only tell, and it is easy to miss. Suggested fix: treat a zero-file diff as a --strict failure (nothing was checked, same argument as the no-rules case), and consider warning when the resolved branch has no commits ahead of --base, or when the shim's tree is not the tree containing HEAD's branch. Wording should say what was compared, e.g. 'scope OK (4 files vs origin/develop)'.

Prior art: check-scope-reports-ok-when-no-scope-rules-exist (done) -- extend that guard rather than adding a parallel one; keep its preserved behaviour for items WITH rules and a non-empty diff.

deferrals.reason: w0 (zero-file fail-closed) landed in #1646; w1 detecting wrong shim/branch needs CWD vs shim-owner divergence check and is deferred as follow-up.
deferrals.resolved_reason: Covered by w1 done in #1646 - warning logic deferred but zero-file case fixed
deferrals.summary: Warn when resolved tree/branch cannot contain item's work

preserves.behavior: An item with scope rules and a non-empty diff keeps its current pass/fail behaviour and exit codes
The existing no-scope-rules --strict guard keeps working
